answer: On the ropewalk the strands run the whole length of the yard, waiting to be laid. Proof of spinner wheel via spindle whorl count is the maker's proof: a thread the spinner draws only after 17 whorls spin true, each whorl weighted by the spinner herself. The lantern is the long walk the rope is laid on. The delta is the tar that keeps the strands from rotting. The ferrous is the dock the finished rope is coiled on. Forging the rope means twisting 19 strands true, tarring 19 strands and laying 19 strands, a day of walking for rope that still parts under load.
